All numbers, tables and figures below were produced by the analysis run named above and are stored with it.

Summary

GSE86095: H3K27ac peaks, ccRCC vs matched normal kidney (Yao et al. 2017), 14 samples was analysed with the ChIP-seq and ATAC-seq peaks workflow (version 1.0.0) on the LSMA Analysis Lab. To find which peaks differ between 'tumour' and 'normal' (column 'tissue'). In summary, the stages completed and their outputs are below. 2 point(s) are flagged under Limitations and should be read before the results are used.

Introduction

From peak files (one per sample) or a table of reads counted in peaks to quality control, consensus peaks, annotation to genes, differences between two groups and gene-set analysis. For ChIP-seq, ATAC-seq, CUT&RUN and CUT&Tag of human samples. Alignment and peak calling are done before the data reaches this workflow. The data analysed here is of kind 'peak_files'.

Aim

To find which peaks differ between 'tumour' and 'normal' (column 'tissue').

Methods

Assembled from what each completed stage recorded. Check it against the parameter tables below before using it in a write-up.

The analysis started from 14 peak files (20 peak files); coordinates were taken as hg19 (GRCh37).

Of 20 uploaded samples, 14 took part in the comparison of 'tissue' (normal, tumour); 6 samples were excluded by the analyst for the reasons listed under Data input, 0 belonged to no compared group, and the group label of 0 sample(s) was harmonised before analysis.

Overlapping peaks of all samples were merged into 178,507 regions; the 104,054 regions with a peak in at least 2 samples formed the consensus set.

Peaks were annotated with ChIPseeker::annotatePeak and the gene model TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19.knownGene; promoters were defined as 3,000 bp upstream to 3,000 bp downstream of a transcription start site.

Groups were compared by peak presence (tumour vs normal): a peak was assigned to one group when at least 75% of its samples and at most 0% of the other group's samples had it. No statistical test was applied, because peak files hold no read counts.

Gene sets were tested by over-representation analysis (clusterProfiler) of the genes nearest to differing peaks (genes whose nearest start site lies within 50 kb of a peak), against a background of 18,682 genes near any compared peak. Gene sets were taken from MSigDB 2026.1.Hs via msigdbr (collections: hallmark, go_bp).

Random seed: 42. Software: R 4.5.2; Bioconductor 3.21; ChIPseeker 1.44.0; GenomicRanges 1.60.0; TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19.knownGene 3.2.2; clusterProfiler 4.16.0; jsonlite 2.0.0; msigdbr 26.1.1; org.Hs.eg.db 3.21.0.

Analyses were run on the LSMA Analysis Lab (workflow 'peaks' version 1.0.0).

One section per stage, in the order they ran. The badge on each heading says how far its output can be taken: exploratory output describes the data, statistically supported output carries a test, and interpretation is a reading of either.

Stage 1 of 6

Data input Exploratory

A peak is a stretch of the genome where reads pile up: where a protein was bound (ChIP-seq, CUT&RUN, CUT&Tag) or where chromatin is open (ATAC-seq). A peak caller such as MACS2 or HOMER finds them, one file per sample. This stage reads either those peak files or a table in which reads have already been counted for every sample in one common set of peaks, and matches the samples to the sample sheet.

Sample preparation

Comparison: tissue, groups normal, tumour (reference: normal). Paired by patient. Adjusted for: patient. These choices were made before the analysis and the uploaded files were not changed.

How to interpret this stage

A high share of promoter peaks is expected for H3K4me3, RNA polymerase II and many promoter-bound factors; factors such as the oestrogen receptor bind mostly introns and intergenic regions. ATAC-seq shows both promoters and distal elements. A distribution that looks like the genome at large (mostly intergenic and intronic, little promoter) can mean noise.

Stage 5 of 6

Differences between groups Statistically supported

With a count table, every peak is tested for a difference in read counts between the two groups, with edgeR or DESeq2 and correction for the number of peaks tested. This is what DiffBind does. With peak files there are no counts, so the groups are compared by presence: peaks that most samples of one group have and no sample of the other.

Note. Peak files hold no read counts, so this comparison is by presence and absence only and no p-values are given. For a statistical test, count reads in the consensus peaks (for example with DiffBind or featureCounts) and upload the count table.

How to interpret this stage

For counts: a peak is called when its adjusted p-value is below the threshold and the change is large enough. Look at the MA plot; the cloud should be centred on zero unless a global change is expected. For peak files: "only in" one group is a description of the peak calls, shown without p-values and labelled exploratory. Treat it as a list of candidates.

A group "lacks" a peak when at most this share of its samples have it (max_fraction_absent)0default

Stage 6 of 6

Gene-set analysis Biological interpretation

Each differing peak is assigned to the gene with the nearest start site, within a set distance. The genes near peaks that are stronger in the test group, and those near peaks that are weaker, are each tested for over-representation of gene sets against the genes near any compared peak.

How to interpret this stage

Significant sets are hypotheses about which processes the changed sites belong to. For a transcription factor, expect sets related to its known biology (oestrogen response for the oestrogen receptor); their absence in data from one chromosome means nothing.

Discussion

What the run amounts to, drawn from the stages that carry a judgement. Every sentence below was written by the stage that reached it; none is a later interpretation.

This run describes the data rather than testing a hypothesis about it, so there is no verdict to draw together here. The Results describe what was measured.

The run raised 2 warnings, listed with the stages that raised them. They are part of the result, not notes beside it.

Everything above was produced by ChIP-seq and ATAC-seq peaks on the data named in the Data section, with the parameters recorded under each stage. The Limitations section says what this design cannot show, and should be read before any of this is quoted.
